units.title: Shelfwise tracks warehouse stock and reserves it for orders
units.claim: Shelfwise tracks how much stock each warehouse holds and reserves stock for incoming orders; it is one deployable TypeScript service with a small admin front end and handles about 3,000 reservations per hour at peak.
units.explanation: Context for the whole canvas.

omission.reason: Context; if the peak figure is shown it stays exact.

units.title: The code is organised in six responsibility groups
units.claim: The modules fall into six responsibility groups: presentation, API and orchestration, domain services, supplier integration, persistence and external systems, and observability and error handling.
units.explanation: The frames of the canvas follow these groups; the frame structure itself carries this idea, not a card.

omission.reason: Represented by the frames (frame_present per group), not by an element.

units.title: The admin UI only talks to the REST API
units.claim: The admin web UI in web/admin/ lets warehouse staff look up stock, place manual holds and review failed imports; it holds no stock logic, calls only the REST API and never talks to the database.
units.explanation: Presentation module and its single dependency.

units.title: HTTP handlers are the only entry point and hold no business rules
units.claim: The HTTP handlers in src/api/routes.ts are the only entry point; they validate the body, attach a correlation ID and pass work on, with no business rules.
units.explanation: API module.

units.title: The reservation orchestrator coordinates ledger, pricing and the StockReserved event
units.claim: POST /reservations goes to the reservation orchestrator in src/orders/reserve.ts, which asks the stock ledger to reserve, asks the pricing rules for the price and, once both succeed, publishes StockReserved to the message broker.
units.explanation: Orchestration module with three outgoing edges.

units.title: No partial reservations: the whole order is rejected
units.claim: If the ledger cannot reserve the full quantity, the orchestrator rejects the whole order and never makes a partial reservation.
units.explanation: A condition on the orchestrator's main claim; stays on the orchestrator element.

units.title: The stock ledger owns stock levels as append-only entries
units.claim: The stock ledger in src/ledger/ledger.ts owns stock levels, records every change as an append-only entry (reserve, release, restock) and writes the entries to Postgres; it is the only module allowed to write the stock tables.
units.explanation: Domain module; sole writer of stock.

units.title: Unconfirmed reservations are released after 15 minutes
units.claim: A reservation that is not confirmed within 15 minutes is released by the ledger and the stock becomes available again.
units.explanation: A condition on the ledger's reservations; stays on the ledger element.

units.title: Pricing rules read cached price lists and never change stock
units.claim: The pricing rules in src/pricing/rules.ts price an order from supplier price lists and active discounts, reading price lists from Redis where they are cached for 300 seconds, and never change stock.
units.explanation: Domain module with a read edge to Redis.

units.title: Dependencies point inwards; domain never depends on HTTP
units.claim: Dependencies point inwards: API calls the orchestrator, the orchestrator calls the domain modules, and the domain modules import nothing from src/api/ or src/orders/ and depend only on persistence and platform helpers, so they stay usable without a web server.
units.explanation: The rule a reversed arrow would break.

units.title: The supplier feed adapter turns supplier deliveries into restocks
units.claim: The supplier feed adapter in src/suppliers/feedAdapter.ts calls the supplier API every 10 minutes for new deliveries, converts each into a restock and asks the stock ledger to record it; it is the only module that knows the supplier's format and the only one that calls the supplier API.
units.explanation: Integration module.

units.title: Unparseable deliveries are logged and skipped, not retried
units.claim: A delivery the adapter cannot parse is logged and skipped, not retried, because sending the same bad data again would fail the same way.
units.explanation: A condition on the adapter; stays on the adapter element.

units.title: Postgres is the source of truth for stock
units.claim: Postgres holds the ledger entries and the current stock level per warehouse and product and is the source of truth for stock; schema changes live in db/migrations/ and run on every deploy.
units.explanation: Persistence.

units.title: Redis holds only rebuildable cached price lists
units.claim: Redis holds cached price lists and nothing that cannot be rebuilt from the supplier feed.
units.explanation: Persistence (cache).

units.title: The message broker carries StockReserved and hosts the dead-letter queue
units.claim: The message broker carries StockReserved events to other services such as fulfilment and hosts the dead-letter queue.
units.explanation: Persistence/messaging.

units.title: The supplier API is the only external system
units.claim: The supplier API is run by the suppliers, outside Shelfwise's control, and is the only external system Shelfwise calls.
units.explanation: External boundary.

units.title: Every module logs through one structured logger
units.claim: Every module logs through the structured logger in src/platform/log.ts, one JSON line per event with the correlation ID the HTTP handlers attached; the handlers log each request and the retry helper each failed attempt.
units.explanation: Observability module.

units.title: The feed adapter wraps supplier calls in the retry helper
units.claim: Calls to the supplier API can fail, so the feed adapter wraps them in the retry helper in src/platform/retry.ts.
units.explanation: Error-handling module.

units.title: Retry policy: 5 attempts, backoff 2 s doubling to 60 s, then inventory.dlq
units.claim: At most 5 attempts per delivery, with exponential backoff starting at 2 seconds, doubling after each failure and capped at 60 seconds; after the 5th failure the delivery is published to the dead-letter queue inventory.dlq on the message broker and staff review it in the admin UI.
units.explanation: The one LLD-level detail: exact values belong in a detail card, not on the module box.

units.title: Only supplier calls are retried; reservations never are
units.claim: Retries apply only to supplier calls; reservations are never retried automatically and a failed reservation is returned to the caller as an error.
units.explanation: Bounds the retry policy; stays with it.

units.title: Start reading at src/orders/reserve.ts, then the ledger
units.claim: New contributors start with src/orders/reserve.ts, which shows a whole reservation in about 120 lines, then src/ledger/ledger.ts; tests sit next to each module's code.
units.explanation: Reading advice.

units.title: Concurrent stock changes rely on an unmeasured row lock
units.claim: The orchestrator and the feed adapter can change the same product's stock at once; the ledger relies on a database row lock, and whether that holds under peak load has not been measured.
units.explanation: An open risk; must not be presented as solved.

units.title: The admin UI has no automated tests
units.claim: The admin UI has no automated tests yet.
units.explanation: Known gap.

units.title: Nothing alerts when inventory.dlq fills up
units.claim: Dead-lettered deliveries are only found when someone opens the admin UI; nothing alerts the team when inventory.dlq fills up.
units.explanation: Known gap.

mustNotClaim.claim: The stock ledger (or pricing rules) depends on, calls or imports the HTTP handlers or the orchestrator.
mustNotClaim.why: Dependencies point inwards; domain modules import nothing from src/api/ or src/orders/.

mustNotClaim.claim: The orchestrator or the feed adapter writes stock to Postgres directly.
mustNotClaim.why: Only the ledger writes stock; the others go through it.
Retries apply only to supplier calls; reservations fail fast.

mustNotClaim.claim: The orchestrator makes partial reservations when stock is short.
Any file path or module the source does not name (for example src/services/, src/db/, a StockRepository class).
mustNotClaim.why: Only the paths written in the source exist in this case.

mustNotClaim.claim: The row lock is proven to hold under peak load.
